title: Build TripMate shared-trip expense tracker
summary: A responsive, private trip ledger that lets groups record pooled funds and expenses, split costs fairly, and understand each member's balance without processing payments.

sources.title: Confirmed technology choices
sources.reference: User confirmed Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, HeroUI, Iconify, and Supabase.

specifications.summary: Private groups can create, join, and configure a trip.
Members can record positive THB contributions into a shared pool.
Members can record personal or shared-pool expenses with an accountable payer.
Expenses can be split equally, among selected members, or as named mixed parts.
The ledger and personal bill show explainable, current balances.
The product is mobile-first and remains convenient on tablet and desktop web.
Only authorised trip members can access private trip data.
The MVP tracks settlements but does not process payments or support multi-currency.

acceptance.summary: An organiser creates a trip with valid required details and receives a private invitation.
A valid invite lets a person join once; invalid, expired, or revoked invitations show an actionable error. Existing members on the same browser return to their trip without another membership.
An organiser can assign a cash holder and start a trip only after at least two members join.
A positive contribution updates the pool balance, contributor total, and activity feed.
A personal or shared-pool expense records its payer, source, and amount; a negative pool balance requires confirmation.
Equal, selected-member, and mixed allocations total exactly to the expense amount and reject invalid participants or allocations.
The active ledger shows current remaining pool balance, total contributed, recent activity, and total used; payer and payment source are available in expense details.
A member's bill itemises allocations, contributions, personal-payment credit, and resulting due or credit position.
The primary flows remain usable on phone, tablet, and desktop widths with accessible controls.
Unauthorised users cannot read or mutate a trip, including through realtime updates.
No payment transfer, currency conversion, or automated settlement action is exposed in the MVP.

contexts.title: Trip setup
contexts.summary: Owns a trip's identity, membership, invitations, status, and cash-holder selection.

glossary.meaning: The member designated to handle the shared-pool workflow; this role does not own other members' money.

contexts.title: Shared ledger
contexts.summary: Owns contributions, expenses, allocations, and the shared-pool balance.

contexts.title: Member position
contexts.summary: Derives each member's explainable trip balance, due amount, or credit from ledger entries.

physicalBoundaries.title: TripMate web application
physicalBoundaries.location: Next.js application deployed as a responsive web app
physicalBoundaries.summary: Renders the experience, coordinates use cases, and performs server-side access-checked data operations.

physicalBoundaries.title: Supabase platform
physicalBoundaries.summary: Provides Auth, Postgres persistence with Row Level Security, and authorised realtime database-change delivery.

infrastructure.title: Next.js App Router
infrastructure.rationale: Provides one responsive web application with server components for data reads, client components for interactive forms, and route handlers/server actions for protected mutations.

infrastructure.title: Tailwind CSS
infrastructure.rationale: Supports mobile-first base utilities with breakpoint overrides for a compact phone UI that expands gracefully to tablet and desktop layouts.

infrastructure.title: HeroUI
infrastructure.rationale: Supplies accessible, Tailwind-compatible form, modal, feedback, and navigation primitives while retaining the custom TripMate visual flow.

infrastructure.title: Iconify
infrastructure.technology: Iconify React with local icon collections
infrastructure.rationale: Provides consistent, accessible icons without hand-drawn assets; selected collections will be bundled locally so core controls do not depend on a third-party icon request at runtime.

infrastructure.title: Supabase Auth
infrastructure.technology: Supabase Auth with Next.js SSR support
infrastructure.rationale: Provides a persistent identity for membership, attribution, and protected sessions without designing a custom credential system.

infrastructure.title: Supabase Postgres and Row Level Security
infrastructure.technology: Postgres migrations and Row Level Security
infrastructure.rationale: Stores the trip ledger durably and enforces member-only reads and writes at the database boundary.

infrastructure.title: Supabase Realtime
infrastructure.rationale: Keeps active trip members informed about new contributions and expenses while applying the same membership access rules.

models.title: Trip
models.summary: A private shared-finance group with its organiser, dates, state, currency, and cash holder.

models.title: Trip membership
models.summary: An active person's membership and role within one private trip.

models.title: Trip invitation
models.summary: A private join token with lifecycle state and expiry.

models.title: Contribution
models.summary: A positive THB amount attributed to a member and added to the shared pool.

models.title: Expense
models.summary: An immutable purchase record with payer, payment source, total THB amount, and allocations.

workflows.title: Set up a private trip group
workflows.summary: An organiser creates a trip, people join through a private invitation, and the group is made ready to track costs.
workflows.goal: A private group has enough authorised members and configuration to start a shared trip ledger.
workflows.diagram: Create trip → Join by invitation → Configure group → Start trip

actions.title: Create a trip
actions.summary: An organiser saves valid trip details and receives a private invitation.
steps: Enter organiser, name, dates, and optional trip details.
Reject missing details or an end date before the start date.
Create the trip, organiser membership, and invitation.
businessRules: A trip name, organiser display name, and valid dates are required.
The MVP trip currency is THB.

serviceRoles.description: Presents the creation form and coordinates the protected trip setup transaction.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses App Router server-side mutation handling for the trip setup transaction.
Uses accessible form controls and validation feedback.
Uses mobile-first layout and wider-screen form arrangement.
Creates the trip, organiser membership, and invitation records under database constraints.

actions.title: Join a trip
actions.summary: An invited person validates an invitation and becomes one active member exactly once.
steps: Restore or automatically create a Supabase anonymous identity; ask new members only for a display name.
Return existing members on the same browser to their trip without creating membership; otherwise reject invalid, expired, or revoked invitations with the agreed message.
Create the membership and show the group board.
businessRules: A person can join a trip only once.
Only a valid private invitation can create membership.

serviceRoles.description: Validates a private join request and renders the resulting group access.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses a route-bound invitation page and protected membership mutation.
Associates the join with a persistent authenticated identity.
Checks invitation state and writes one membership under Row Level Security.

actions.details: Existing-member access uses authenticated membership and does not depend on an invitation still being valid. New joins with invalid, expired or revoked invitations show: “This invitation is no longer valid. Ask the organiser for a new link.” No visible registration form is required.

actions.title: Configure and start the group
actions.summary: The organiser assigns a cash holder and starts a sufficiently populated trip.
steps: Review joined members on the group board.
Select a current member as the cash holder.
Keep Start trip disabled below two active members including the organiser; allow only the organiser to start once the threshold is met.
businessRules: Only the organiser can set the cash holder or start the trip.
A trip needs at least two active members before it starts.

serviceRoles.description: Enforces organiser-only group configuration and shows the group board.

infrastructureLinks.description: Coordinates the role-checked start transition.
Reads active membership and stores the cash-holder and trip status changes.
Refreshes the group board when other invited members join.

records.title: Trip group
records.summary: Created during setup and read when people join or the organiser starts the trip.

workflows.verification: Plan unit validation for dates, invitation lifecycle, duplicate membership, organiser permissions, and start conditions; integration coverage for Row Level Security; E2E coverage for create, join, and start on a responsive browser.

workflows.title: Maintain the shared trip ledger
workflows.summary: Members contribute funds and record shared costs while everyone sees a current, access-controlled ledger.
workflows.goal: The group has an accurate shared-pool balance and visible record of spending.
workflows.diagram: Add funds → Record expense → Update ledger → Review activity

actions.title: Add a pool contribution
actions.summary: A member records a positive THB contribution and immediately sees its ledger effect.
steps: Choose the contributor and enter a positive THB amount with an optional note.
Reject a zero, negative, or malformed amount.
Save the contribution and publish the updated activity.
businessRules: A contribution amount must be greater than zero.
A contribution is attributed to one active trip member.

serviceRoles.description: Collects a contribution form and coordinates an authorised ledger write.

infrastructureLinks.description: Runs the protected contribution use case from the responsive UI.
Provides accessible money input and save feedback.
Stores the contribution for an authorised trip member.
Delivers the new ledger entry to authorised active viewers.

actions.title: Record and split an expense
actions.summary: A member records the payer, payment source, amount, and a valid allocation in one immutable ledger entry.
steps: Enter the expense description, payer, source, and positive THB total.
Choose everyone, selected-member, or mixed allocation and preview every person's exact share before saving.
Reject empty participants, negative shares, or allocations that do not equal the total.
Warn with the resulting negative pool balance and require explicit Save anyway confirmation; Cancel leaves the expense unsaved.
Save the expense and allocations as one ledger entry.
businessRules: An expense total and every allocation must be positive.
Allocations must sum exactly to the expense total after deterministic displayed rounding.
A personal payer receives credit so the same shared cost is not charged twice.

serviceRoles.description: Guides a member through entry, pre-save allocation validation, and authorised immutable ledger writing.

infrastructureLinks.description: Coordinates the protected expense transaction and negative-pool confirmation flow.
Uses accessible selection, disclosure, and confirmation controls.
Supplies labelled visual affordances for payer, pool, split, and warning states.
Stores each immutable expense and its allocations atomically under membership policy.
Delivers the changed ledger state to authorised subscribed members.

actions.details: All split modes preview exact person-level allocations. For ฿121 split among three people, show ฿40.34, ฿40.33 and ฿40.33 with deterministic remainder assignment. Mixed splits show how the parts produce each person's share.

actions.title: Review the active ledger
actions.summary: A member sees the current pool balance, total used, payment sources, and recent activity.
steps: Confirm the viewer is an active trip member.
Read contributions and expenses for the trip.
Show remaining pool balance prominently, total contributed separately, total used and recent activity; open an expense to see its payer and payment source.
Apply authorised realtime changes to the displayed ledger.
businessRules: Only active trip members can view a trip ledger.
Shared-pool expenses reduce pool balance; personal expenses do not.

serviceRoles.description: Renders a member-scoped ledger and keeps it current without exposing unauthorised records.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses server data reads for the initial ledger view and client interactivity for live refresh.
Presents a compact phone ledger that expands into efficient wider-screen information layout.
Reads only trip records permitted by Row Level Security.
Receives authorised changes for the active trip.

records.title: Shared ledger
records.summary: Contributions and expenses are written by members and summarised for viewers.

workflows.verification: Plan unit tests for money validation, allocation and balance calculations; integration tests for atomic persisted expense/allocation writes, RLS, and authorised realtime subscription; E2E coverage for contribution, each split mode, negative-pool confirmation, and responsive ledger review.

workflows.title: Understand a member's trip position
workflows.summary: A member opens an itemised bill and uses the shared ledger to understand their due or credit position without a payment flow.
workflows.goal: Every member can explain their net trip position from recorded entries.
workflows.diagram: Open personal bill → Calculate position → Review itemised totals

actions.title: View a personal bill
actions.summary: A member views their allocations, paid-into-pool total, personal payer credit, and net due or credit.
steps: Confirm the viewer is an active trip member.
Read the viewer's allocations, contributions, and personally paid shared expenses.
Calculate an itemised shared-cost total, pool contribution total, payer credit, and net position.
Display the itemised bill with a clear due or credit label and a separate “Paid personally” credit row when applicable.
businessRules: A bill total must be traceable to ledger entries.
The MVP presents settlement information but never initiates payment.

serviceRoles.description: Calculates and renders an authorised member's explainable view of the trip ledger.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses an authenticated trip route to load and render the bill.
Keeps the bill readable from narrow phone screens through desktop widths.
Reads only ledger records visible to the authenticated member through Row Level Security.

actions.title: Review shared context
actions.summary: A member returns to the active ledger to reconcile bill line items with the trip's shared activity.
steps: Open the active ledger from the bill.
Match bill items to visible activity and expense details.
Return to the bill with the shared context understood.

serviceRoles.description: Connects the personal bill and ledger views without creating a settlement transaction.

infrastructureLinks.description: Provides the protected navigation and data views.
Provides labelled navigation and information icons where helpful.

records.title: Member bill
records.summary: A derived view built from ledger records for one active member.

workflows.verification: Plan unit tests for net-position calculations and no-payment boundaries; integration tests for member-scoped bill reads; E2E coverage for an itemised bill that traces back to ledger activity across phone and desktop widths.

testCases.title: Create a valid THB trip and invitation
testCases.given: An authenticated organiser enters complete valid details.
testCases.then: A draft THB trip, organiser membership, and active invitation exist.

testCases.title: Reject invalid trip dates
testCases.given: The end date precedes the start date.
testCases.then: It reports the date error and creates no trip.

testCases.title: Join once with a valid invitation
testCases.given: An authenticated person has an active invitation.
testCases.when: They join with a display name.
testCases.then: Exactly one active membership is created.

testCases.title: Refuse unusable invitation joins
testCases.given: A new join uses an invalid, expired, or revoked invitation.
testCases.then: No membership is created; show: This invitation is no longer valid. Ask the organiser for a new link.

testCases.title: Require two members and organiser authority to start
testCases.given: The request is from a non-organiser or the trip has fewer than two members.
testCases.then: The status remains draft.

testCases.title: Save a valid contribution
testCases.given: An authorised member enters a positive THB amount.
testCases.then: The record, pool balance, contributor total, and activity update together.

testCases.title: Reject non-positive contribution amounts
testCases.given: An amount is zero, negative, or malformed.
testCases.then: No contribution is saved.

testCases.title: Record a personal shared expense
testCases.given: A member paid a positive personal expense for the group.
testCases.then: The expense retains its personal source and payer without reducing pool balance.

testCases.title: Require confirmation for a negative shared pool
testCases.given: A shared-pool expense exceeds the available balance.
testCases.then: Show the resulting shortfall and require Save anyway; Cancel or absence of confirmation does not save.

testCases.title: Split equally with deterministic rounding
testCases.given: ฿121 is split equally among three active members.
testCases.then: Shares are ฿40.34, ฿40.33 and ฿40.33 in deterministic order, and the exact shares are shown before save.

testCases.title: Reject invalid selected and mixed splits
testCases.given: A split has no selected people, a negative allocation, or allocations not equal to the total.
testCases.then: The expense cannot be saved.

testCases.title: Show an authorised live ledger
testCases.given: Two authorised members have an active trip.
testCases.then: The other sees the authorised updated ledger state.

testCases.title: Block non-member trip access
testCases.given: An authenticated user is not a trip member.
testCases.when: They attempt a protected read or write.
testCases.then: Row Level Security and the application deny access.

testCases.title: Calculate an explainable personal bill
testCases.given: A ledger with shared allocations, contributions, and personal payer credits.
testCases.then: It returns itemised totals and the correct net due or credit.

testCases.title: Keep settlement display-only
testCases.then: The MVP exposes no payment transfer, currency conversion, or automated settlement control.

testCases.title: Use the main flows across responsive widths
testCases.given: Phone, tablet, and desktop viewport fixtures.
testCases.then: Controls remain reachable, readable, and keyboard accessible at each viewport.

testCases.title: Start a configured group with two members
testCases.given: An organiser has a draft trip with two active members.
testCases.when: They select a cash holder and start the trip.
testCases.then: The cash holder is saved and the trip becomes active.

testCases.title: Returning anonymous member reopens their existing trip
testCases.given: The same browser retains an anonymous session and active trip membership.
testCases.then: Return the existing trip without inserting another membership, even if the invitation is no longer usable for new joins.

testCases.title: Preview selected-member and mixed shares exactly
testCases.then: Each included member has an exact share, excluded members are not charged, and every part and total reconcile.

testCases.title: Present agreed ledger and bill details
testCases.given: ฿2,000 contributed and ฿761 paid from the pool, plus a personal-payment fixture.
testCases.when: The member reviews the ledger, opens an expense and views their bill.
testCases.then: Ledger shows ฿1,239 remaining and ฿2,000 contributed separately; payer and source appear in details; bill shows Paid personally credit.

choices: Selected: a single Next.js TypeScript responsive web application is the MVP delivery shape, rather than separate native apps, because the product must work conveniently on phone, tablet, and desktop web from one codebase.
Selected: Tailwind CSS provides mobile-first styling; unprefixed utilities target phones and breakpoint variants expand the layout for wider screens.
Selected: HeroUI supplies accessible UI primitives, customised with Tailwind to follow the supplied design rather than replacing it with a generic component-library appearance.
Selected: Iconify is used only where an icon improves comprehension; core icon collections are bundled locally to avoid a runtime dependency on an icon API.
Selected: Supabase supplies persistent authentication, Postgres, Row Level Security, and authorised realtime updates, avoiding a separate custom backend for the MVP.
Deferred: payment processing, payment-provider compliance, multi-currency, notifications, receipt capture, and settlement write actions remain outside this plan.
Confirmed UX: anonymous Supabase Auth behind a display-name-only join; same-browser members return directly to their existing trip.
Confirmed UX: remaining pool balance is primary, total contributed is separate; payer and source appear in expense details only.
Confirmed UX: preview exact per-person shares for all split modes; include Paid personally credit when applicable; allow pool overdraft only through explicit Save anyway confirmation.
constraints: The repository currently contains the design and PRD but no application code; the plan therefore proposes the initial application architecture rather than extending an established implementation.
All persisted money values use THB decimal precision; calculations must preserve exact displayed totals and deterministic rounding.
Trip data is private. Database Row Level Security is a required enforcement layer, not just a UI convention.
Realtime delivery must never bypass membership authorisation.
No payments are initiated, requested, or processed in the MVP.
